reply_text:
I found three new 2024 claims, but none comes from a source in Lee's own unedited words. Two were said at Fortune's Innovation Forum in Hong Kong in March 2024. I only saw them in a Fortune news article published 25 May, so they are coverage_only. The third is from an edited, translated Q&A from 36Kr's WISE2024 summit in late November.

- **50% of jobs by 2027 (March).** Asked whether his 2017 forecast still holds with three years left, he said "It's actually uncannily accurate." His quoted words don't name 2027 themselves; the interviewer's question supplies the date. Treat it as a 2024 restatement of a 2017 forecast.
- **AI faking empathy, next 50 years (March).** He said people won't accept AI that fakes compassion "for the next 50 years." This is about whether people will accept AI, not about what AI can do, so it's a borderline case.
- **Model costs (November).** He said there is a "99% chance" that models seen as too expensive won't be next year, and that a year after that they would support the applications people want.

**Not candidates:**
- The Diamandis podcast (5 December 2024) is said to contain "AGI in 5–10 years." I only read that on a third-party summary page with no direct quote, and that page also mentions an event from 2025, so I didn't trust it. It may be the same claim as your existing October 2024 AGI file.
- At WISE2024 he also said "Over the next year, I'm most optimistic about applications." That is close to your 26 November "flood of apps in 2025" files, but it reads as optimism rather than a dated prediction, so I left it out.

**Pages that didn't open:** The Washington Post transcript of the June Futurist Summit and Nicholas Thompson's LinkedIn transcript of the January Davos panel both failed. I quote nothing from them; they are the best leads for a follow-up pass. I used all 6 page openings and 7 of the 12 searches.
